topics.title: 1 How and why did the United States develop as an independent nation?

outcomes.text: Explain colonists’ responses to British rule from 1754 to 1776.
Describe the Articles of Confederation.
Explain how the Constitution was created.
Identify the creation and main provisions of the Bill of Rights.
Describe the presidency’s role before 1830.
Compare the Federalist, Democratic and Whig parties.
Explain the ideas and effects of Jacksonian Democracy.

topics.title: 2 Why had the borders of the United States changed so much by 1853?

outcomes.text: Describe the French and Indian War of 1754.
Explain foreign powers’ roles in the Revolutionary War from 1775 to 1783.
Explain the significance of the Louisiana Purchase in 1803.
Describe the War of 1812 and its impact.
Explain Spain’s declining influence and the acquisition of Florida in 1819.
Describe the annexation of Texas from 1845 to 1846.
Explain the 1846 treaty settling the Canadian border.
Explain the war and peace settlement with Mexico from 1846 to 1853, including Guadalupe Hidalgo.

topics.title: 3 How and why did the lives of the Native Americans change?

outcomes.text: Describe Native American relations with colonists before independence and the Pontiac Rebellion.
Explain Tecumseh’s Confederacy.
Explain Andrew Jackson’s Indian Removal Act of 1830.
Assess westward expansion’s impact on Native Americans.
Describe the Sand Creek Massacre, Red River War and Little Bighorn.
Explain the Reservation System and Dawes Act of 1887.
Explain the Battle of Wounded Knee in 1890 and its effects.

topics.title: 4 What were the causes and consequences of the Civil War?

outcomes.text: Explain attempts to compromise over slavery, including Missouri, 1850 and Kansas–Nebraska.
Explain rising tensions involving Republicans, the South, Dred Scott and John Brown.
Describe the Lincoln–Douglas Debates of 1858.
Explain Lincoln’s election and Southern secession in 1860–61.
Describe Reconstruction measures, including the Freedmen’s Bureau and Black Codes.
Explain the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments.
Describe the Enforcement Acts, Slaughter House Cases and 1876 compromise.
Explain the development of Jim Crow laws.

topics.title: 5 How, and with what effects, did the economy change after 1850?

outcomes.text: Explain Northern industrialization through factories, output and inventions.
Assess railroads’ effects on the economy and communities.
Describe urban housing, sanitation, child labour and factory conditions.
Explain the development of the National Labor Union, Knights of Labor and AFL.
Explain the Farmers’ Alliance and Populism.

topics.title: 6 What was the impact of immigration after 1850?

outcomes.text: Explain immigration pull factors, including liberty and economic opportunity.
Explain the Homestead Act of 1862.
Describe increased Mexican immigration after 1850.
Explain changing immigration from Central, Southern and Eastern Europe.
Describe Chinese railway workers and the Chinese Exclusion Act.
Describe Japanese workers’ migration to Hawaii from 1885.
Assess immigrant customs and culture’s effects on major cities.
Explain tensions between immigrant communities, stereotypes and prejudices.
Describe anti-immigration groups, including the American Party, Know Nothings and Ku Klux Klan.

topics.title: 2 Was the 1920s a “boom” time for all Americans?

outcomes.text: Explain Republican policies supporting the 1920s boom, including tariffs, Normalcy and laissez-faire.
Describe postwar prosperity through productivity, wages, credit, marketing and consumerism.
Explain industrial expansion through electricity, appliances, motor production and assembly lines.
Assess changes and continuities in women’s lives, including the New Woman.
Describe farmers’ and farm labourers’ economic conditions.
Explain the boom’s effects on textiles, coal mining and different regions.

topics.title: 3 Why did the Great Depression happen and with what consequences for the United States?

outcomes.text: Explain causes of the 1929 Crash, including overproduction, debt, speculation and margin buying.
Describe Depression poverty through Hoovervilles, the Dust Bowl, family impacts and discrimination.
Assess Hoover’s recovery policies, including Hoover Dam and the RFC.
Describe the First Hundred Days and New Deal measures for finance, relief, jobs and regulation.
Explain Second New Deal agencies, rural electrification and Social Security.
Assess the New Deal’s limitations for women and African Americans.

topics.title: 4 How did the lives of African Americans change during the period from 1890 to 1970?

outcomes.text: Describe African Americans’ status in 1890, including Jim Crow and lynching.
Explain Booker T. Washington’s ideas and the Atlanta Compromise.
Explain Plessy v. Ferguson and its significance.
Describe Du Bois’s work and the NAACP.
Explain the Great Migration and Harlem Renaissance.
Describe challenges to Jim Crow during the 1950s and early 1960s.
Explain the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965.
Explain Martin Luther King’s use of nonviolent protest.
Describe radical Black activism through Malcolm X, Black Power and the Black Panthers.

topics.title: 5 How did the United States manage its relationship with the rest of the world after 1945?

outcomes.text: Explain the aims and outcomes of the Yalta and Potsdam conferences.
Describe the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan.
Explain containment through the Berlin Airlift, Korean War and Vietnam War.
Explain changing US–Soviet relations through nuclear rivalry, Cuba, arms control, détente and Able Archer.

subtopics.title: Reagan and the Cold War’s End

outcomes.text: Assess Reagan’s role in ending the Cold War.

topics.title: 6 How did the United States deal with domestic challenges after 1945?

outcomes.text: Explain McCarthyism through congressional hearings and HUAC.
Describe postwar economic growth, including restructuring, conglomerates, franchises and McDonald’s.
Explain Kennedy’s New Frontier and Johnson’s Great Society.
Explain Vietnam War effects on inflation and deficit spending.
Describe the oil crisis, Carter’s energy plan and the nuclear energy debate.
Explain Reaganomics.
